english: Let $p$ and $q$ be real numbers and let $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that $F(-2)=0$ and $F'(x)=\dfrac{px+q}{x^{2}+4x+13}$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Suppose that the function $F(x)-\log_{e}\left(x^{2}+4x+13\right)$ is bounded on $\mathbb{R}$ and that $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\left(F(x)-F(-x)\right)=\pi$. Then $F(1)$ is equal to
hindi: माना कि $p$ तथा $q$ वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं तथा $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ एक अवकलनीय फलन है जिसके लिए $F(-2)=0$ तथा सभी $x\in\mathbb{R}$ के लिए $F'(x)=\dfrac{px+q}{x^{2}+4x+13}$ है। माना कि फलन $F(x)-\log_{e}\left(x^{2}+4x+13\right)$, $\mathbb{R}$ पर परिबद्ध है तथा $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\left(F(x)-F(-x)\right)=\pi$ है। तब $F(1)$ बराबर है
solution: Bounded difference: the $\tan^{-1}$ part is bounded, so $\dfrac p2=1\Rightarrow p=2$
$F(x)-F(-x)$: the log parts differ by $\log_{e}\dfrac{x^{2}+4x+13}{x^{2}-4x+13}\to 0$; the $\tan^{-1}$ parts give $\dfrac{q-4}{3}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$
solution_full: Write the numerator in terms of the derivative of the denominator: $px+q=\dfrac p2(2x+4)+(q-2p)$.

$F(x)-\log_{e}\left(x^{2}+4x+13\right)=\left(\dfrac p2-1\right)\log_{e}\left(x^{2}+4x+13\right)+\dfrac{q-2p}{3}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x+2}{3}+C$. The $\tan^{-1}$ term is bounded and the log term is unbounded as $x\to\infty$, so boundedness forces $\dfrac p2=1$, i.e. $p=2$.
As $x\to\infty$ the ratio inside the logarithm tends to $1$, while $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x+2}{3}\to\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2-x}{3}\to-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. So the limit is $\dfrac{q-4}{3}\pi$.
Setting it equal to $\pi$: $q-4=3$, so $q=7$, and $F(x)=\log_{e}\left(x^{2}+4x+13\right)+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x+2}{3}+C$.
originality_note: New: the two unknown coefficients are fixed by asymptotic conditions on the antiderivative itself: boundedness of F minus a log fixes the log coefficient, and the limit of F(x) - F(-x) isolates the arctan coefficient because the log parts cancel at infinity (way 5). Closest known: integral of (px+q)/(ax^2+bx+c) by splitting the numerator. Different because: the solver must see which part of the antiderivative survives each condition.
key_step: Splitting the numerator, then using boundedness for p and the odd-part limit for q (log terms cancel, arctan terms add).
justification: Standard integral form, but the two coefficients are recovered from limit behaviour of the antiderivative, which needs care with which terms survive. Two ideas linked, options help; comparable to 2025-P2-Q1 (L2) limit-with-a-given-function raised to L3 by the two-condition setup, near 2023-P2-Q3 (L3).

concept_use.Integrals of the form int dx/(ax^2+bx+c): The part q - 2p over (x+2)^2 + 9 integrates to ((q-2p)/3) tan^-1((x+2)/3), whose limits at plus and minus infinity give q = 7.
concept_use.Integrals of the form int (px+q)/(ax^2+b: The numerator is split as (p/2)(2x+4) + (q-2p) so the first part integrates to (p/2) ln(x^2+4x+13); boundedness then gives p = 2.
